test_policy.notes: OU has permanently removed the standardized-test requirement for first-year admission (applicants need a 2.5 minimum GPA). Scores may be sent to support scholarship eligibility and course placement. Admission is based on cumulative GPA of 3.2+ (2.5 to 3.19 may be admitted after review of preparation), course quality and grade trend.

requirements.notes: Own online application; no essay or recommendation letters required (essay optional). International applicants submit transcripts (literal English translation if not in English; unofficial copies accepted for first-year), English test scores and financial documents. Application fee: the Common Data Set answers No; the admissions pages checked do not mention a fee. Direct admission to Nursing (BSN) applies by Oct 31 of senior year; music, theatre and dance majors require an audition.

deadlines.label: International application deadline, fall 2027
deadlines.notes: The page says to submit the completed application by July 1 for fall (Nov 1 winter, Mar 1 summer); no year is printed, so fall 2027 is assumed. Admission is rolling with decisions beginning July 1 per the Common Data Set. Completed applications can be deferred up to one year.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Required for international applicants, other visa holders, permanent residents and applicants whose first language is not English, unless they have one year of study and a diploma from a U.S. high school; a full high school diploma earned at a non-U.S. school taught entirely in English; 24 transferable credits (excluding ESL) from a U.S. college; a degree from a regionally accredited U.S. college; or completion of ELS Level 112. Some programs require higher English levels. Oakland also has the Global Achievement Pathways Program (GAPP), which admits students to a degree with lower English scores while they take ESL classes for one or two semesters (viewbook: for example TOEFL iBT 69-78 one semester, 62-68 two semesters; Duolingo 95 one semester, 90 two; PTE 48-52 one semester, 44-47 two); lower scores go to the ESL Institute first.

english.notes: For exams before Jan. 20, 2026 (0-120 scale). GAPP: 69-78 needs one semester of ESL alongside courses, 62-68 two semesters (viewbook).
For exams on or after Jan. 21, 2026 (1-6 scale).
IELTS Indicator copies are also accepted for the application. Viewbook GAPP route starts at IELTS 6.0 (minimum section 5.5) with one semester of ESL.
GAPP: 95 one semester of ESL, 90 two semesters (viewbook).
PTE Academic. GAPP: 48-52 one semester of ESL, 44-47 two semesters (viewbook).

cost.notes: International page estimate (fall and winter, 12-14 credits per semester): out-of-state tuition $19,788, living expenses $11,454 (entered under room and board), medical insurance $2,292 (under other), total $33,534; budget about $4,000 more for books and personal costs. $15,426 is the in-state-equivalent tuition shown for Canadian/Mexican students with the Non-Resident Award. The page does not date this table. 2026-27 per-credit rates: non-resident lower division $795.75 (upper $853.25); Michigan lower division $574.50. OU charges no mandatory fees

aid.notes: OU's scholarship page says international students are not eligible for OU scholarships except where noted; the Non-Resident Award (in-state tuition rate) goes to U.S. out-of-state students and to citizens and permanent residents of Canada and Mexico with a 2.5+ GPA, who must live on campus two years. The international viewbook nevertheless says competitive scholarships for international students exist and the Common Data Set shows 127 nonresidents received institutional non-need-based aid (average $5,851), but no international award amounts are published.

toefl.note: The pages read do not print a TOEFL institution code; look it up in the ETS code search.
